title: P0 Customer escalation: memory-cascade OOMs across Hosted/Dedicated/Private - mitigation + runtime patch plan
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Over the past 48 hours we saw repeated GPU OOMs and sudden runtime OOM cascades affecting hosted tenants and two Dedicated clusters; one Private deployment also reported degraded throughput. Root cause hypothesis is an interaction of (1) an allocator accounting bug under long-lived sessions with large per-session KV caches causing underreported live allocation, (2) a race in KV handle eviction that temporarily leaves dangling references preventing slab coalescing, and (3) amplified fragmentation from mixed-size tensor allocations. Impact: production latency spikes, failed requests, and three customer escalations (one Sev2).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:14 - Maya Chen: Initial triage - OOMs started after a high-throughput inference spike; affected both hosted multi-tenant pools and two Dedicated nodes. Gathering core dumps and GPU traces.

2026-03-10 12:02 - Diego Alvarez: Found repeated 'kv_handle->refcount' spikes before OOM; slab external fragmentation metric rising steadily. Hypothesis: KV eviction left stale pointers that prevented arena free merging.

2026-03-10 15:47 - Priya Patel (SRE): Applied emergency mitigations to Hosted: limited per-session KV size to 128MB and enabled conservative batch throttling. Early results: hosted OOMs reduced by 70% but Dedicated still experiences bursts.

2026-03-11 08:30 - Diego Alvarez: Built PoC runtime patch: (A) make KV eviction atomic and introduce tombstone sweep that clears dangling refs before freeing, (B) add allocator backpressure on per-session KV growth, (C) opportunistic slab coalescer that runs during GC pauses. Patch under review in PR#4301.

2026-03-11 13:55 - QA (Lara Ng): Integration smoke results: patch prevents OOM in long-tail synthetic workload but increases short-term latency ~5% under peak — acceptable for emergency rollout with rollback plan.

2026-03-12 09:00 - Customer Success: Notified three customers about mitigation steps and upcoming runtime hotfix rollout window on 2026-03-13 02:00 UTC. One customer requested canary on their Dedicated pool first.

2026-03-12 11:20 - Diego Alvarez: Plan approved by Eng Leads; preparing canary image and automated rollback scenarios. Post-deploy observability: token-level error rate, slab-fragmentation gauge, kv-live-bytes per session.

2026-03-12 16:45 - Maya Chen: Post-mortem checklist items drafted; follow-ups include improved telemetry for refcount regressions and a regression test harness to simulate mixed-size tensor allocation patterns.
acceptance_criteria: No new GPU OOMs attributable to allocator/kv interactions for 72h in canary and 48h in production after rollout
Per-session KV live bytes metrics align with accounting (drift < 2%) across 95th pctile sessions
Slab fragmentation metric decreases by >= 30% under long-tail workload in controlled tests
Customer escalations acknowledged and status updated; Dedicated customer canary successful
implementation_plan: 1) Emergency mitigations (done): limit per-session KV to 128MB hosted, throttle batch ingress for highest-throughput routes
2) Patch: make KV eviction atomic, add tombstone sweep pass, add allocator accounting fix and opportunistic slab coalescer (PR#4301)
3) Canary rollout: Dedicated customer pool first (01:00 UTC 2026-03-13) with synthetic regen traffic and live telemetry
4) Gradual rollout to hosted pools with 10% -> 30% -> 100% progression with 1-hour observation gates
5) Post-deploy verification: run regression harness, validate metrics and replay failing traces
6) Postmortem and permanent tests: add fuzz tests for KV eviction races and long-tail tensor mix scenarios
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Patch increases short-tail latency under peak traffic. Mitigation: enable conservative rollout and revert path; monitor P95 latency and error rates with automatic rollback threshold.
Risk: Tombstone sweep CPU overhead. Mitigation: make sweep incremental and budgeted; run during GC windows and idle cycles.
Risk: Canary uncovers new memory regression. Mitigation: keep one Dedicated standby and rapid rollback image ready; notify affected customers.
Risk: Customers on Private may be slow to accept upgrades. Mitigation: provide backported minimal hotfix and runbook for assisted upgrade with SRE on-call.
next_steps: Merge PR#4301 after one more review from runtime team (action: Diego)
Schedule canary window with Dedicated customer (action: Maya & CS)
Prepare rollback image and run automated canary checks (action: SRE)
Create postmortem doc and link to incident page (action: Maya)
Add two regression tests to CI that reproduce the memory-cascade pattern (action: Eng Reliability)
